title: LAUNCH_PLAN
universal_lens: The launch plan formalizes a two-stage temporal optimization over a decaying attention manifold. Phase A accumulates empirical priors (ADP receipts) to minimize posterior uncertainty, while Phase B executes a high-leverage state transition at the NFL kickoff singularity, maximizing conversion density.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats early-season ADP as noisy observations of latent talent. The soft-launch phase gathers sufficient statistics to calibrate conformal prediction sets. Only when backtested coverage thresholds are met does the system unlock the full in-season projection suite.
gse_mapping: GSE models the user funnel as a Markov Decision Process. The $49 founding tier acts as an absorbing state for early adopters. The engine transitions from pre-draft best-ball utilities to dynamic in-season start/sit kernels based on real-time injury and matchup states.

primitives.name: Preseason Attention Gradient
primitives.verbatim_quote: NFL 2026: **HOF Game Aug 6 · Preseason Wk1 Aug 13 · Kickoff Sept 9.** The closer to kickoff, the more draft-hungry the audience — and the less runway to fill the funnel.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t: time (days), K: kickoff singularity, A(t): audience attention (dimensionless probability mass), R(t): conversion runway (dimensionless capacity).
primitives.assumptions: Audience attention follows a convex acceleration curve approaching the season start; funnel capacity is strictly bounded by calendar constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If t approaches K without sufficient prior accumulation, R(t) collapses to zero, rendering paid or organic acquisition infinitely costly.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's pre-season data sparsity problem. Early low-signal windows must be leveraged to build priors before the high-noise regular season begins.
layer2.telemetry: Weekly active users (WAU) and draft tool engagement rates leading up to September.

primitives.name: Calibration-Gated Release Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Phase B — Loud kickoff (around Sept 9).** Flip the owned weekly-projection model live (only after its backtest clears), which unlocks the full in-season suite (start/sit, waivers, trade).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: M: projection model, C(M): calibration score (Brier score / ECE), T: threshold clearance, S: feature suite state (binary).
primitives.assumptions: Model reliability is non-negotiable; feature exposure is strictly conditional on passing rigorous out-of-sample backtesting.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If C(M) > T at kickoff, the release is delayed, causing a catastrophic loss of momentum against competing fantasy platforms.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSI's conformal inference pipeline. The 'loud kickoff' is only permitted when the prediction intervals achieve nominal coverage on holdout data.
layer2.telemetry: Backtest Brier scores, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), and subsequent user retention post-launch.

primitives.name: Founding Pricing Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Pricing benchmark: credible fantasy-tools subscriptions cluster ~$40–$100/yr (FantasyPros MVP $71.88, Fantasy Life+ T2 $99.99, 4for4 Pro $59, RotoViz ~$60) — $49 founding undercuts the band while clearly beating "free Sleeper" on decision tools.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P_f: founding price ($49), P_m: market distribution of competitor prices, V_d: delta value over free baseline.
primitives.assumptions: Price elasticity is highly sensitive near the zero-price anchor (free apps); lifetime value (LTV) is secured via grandfathering guarantees.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If P_f exceeds the lower bound of P_m significantly, or if V_d is perceived as negligible, conversion elasticity drops precipitously.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's value extraction layer. The pricing kernel establishes a permanent discount factor for early supporters, locking in long-term revenue streams ahead of equilibrium pricing.
layer2.telemetry: Conversion rate from free trial to Founding tier, churn rate compared to industry benchmarks.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Galaxy Fantasy launch plan is fundamentally a constrained optimization problem over a finite temporal horizon defined by the NFL calendar. We define the objective function as maximizing the product of audience attention A(t) and conversion probability C(t). The 'soft-launch' (Phase A) operates in a regime of high data sparsity but low competitive friction. Mathematically, this is an exploration phase where the system accumulates empirical priors—specifically Average Draft Position (ADP) receipts—to refine the underlying probabilistic engine. The 'loud kickoff' (Phase B) represents the exploitation phase, triggered precisely at the temporal singularity of Week 1. The critical duality lies in the gating mechanism: the release of advanced features (start/sit, waivers) is not merely a marketing toggle but a strict function of the model's calibration metrics. If the backtested Expected Calibration Error (ECE) exceeds a predefined threshold, the transition is vetoed, preventing brand degradation. The pricing primitive introduces a permanent discount factor, effectively locking in a higher Net Present Value (NPV) for early adopters by exploiting the psychological anchoring effect against the zero-cost baseline of free platforms like Sleeper. The entire architecture relies on the assumption that early, transparent data sharing (read-only syncs) builds sufficient trust capital to survive the inevitable noise of preseason injuries and roster fluctuations.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This strategy echoes the historical shift in quantitative finance from black-box proprietary models to transparent, API-driven risk engines. Just as early Bloomberg terminals offered raw data feeds before complex derivatives pricing, Galaxy uses basic draft tools to establish infrastructure dominance. It also mirrors the open-source software paradigm, where a free/core utility builds a massive user base that subsidizes the development of premium, high-margin enterprise features.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The primary agent is the fantasy football manager, modeled as a bounded rational actor seeking cognitive offloading. They are overwhelmed by data volume and seek a trusted oracle to minimize regret in draft decisions. Competitors (RotoViz, 4for4) are viewed as established incumbents with entrenched user habits. The launch plan exploits the manager's anxiety regarding the upcoming season, positioning the $49 tier as a low-risk insurance policy against poor performance, leveraging loss aversion to drive conversions before the season starts.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists between the marketing timeline and the statistical validation layer. If the GSI calibration metrics fail to clear the backtest threshold by late August, the 'loud kickoff' must be aborted or pivoted to a purely content-led campaign. Allowing uncalibrated projections to go live would introduce catastrophic leakage, destroying the core value proposition ('the only fantasy projection that publishes its own calibration') and rendering the pricing kernel worthless due to immediate churn.
